\section{Introduction}
Neural machine translation quality drops sharply
when parallel sentences are scarce.
We study how far monolingual text in the target language
can close the gap for a language pair with only ninety thousand parallel sentences.

\section{Model}
The encoder produces hidden states $h_1$, $h_2$ and $h_3 for each source token,
which the decoder attends over while generating the translation.

We initialise both sides from a multilingual pretrained model
and fine-tune on a mix of parallel and back-translated data.
The back-translation weight is annealed over the first half of training.
